chapter: Part Two: theaters and the Chicago scene
title: Dave Peyton's band at the Regal
summary: Peyton led from piano; stage by Fess Williams; mostly newsreels and stock arrangements.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Right. And the band played on stage as well as in the pit?
No, not at the Met.
Not at the Met? That was at the Regal?
That was at the Regal.
Same band at the Regal?
No, just another band.
Was it Tate's band?
No, this was Dave Payton's band.
Oh, Dave Payton.
Dave Payton directed the band, and Fess Williams directed the band on stage. Hewas the master of ceremony.
Was Dave Payton, and Tate, they were more like businessmen, weren't they?
Yeah.
But were they also good musicians?
Yeah, they were good musicians. Erskine Tate played violin. Of course, Dave Payton played piano.
Did he play piano in the band?
Yeah.
And he directed from --
He directed from the piano.
Who did the arranging in Peyton's band?
Let me see. I can't remember who did the arranging. We didn't have many arrangements in Dave Peyton's band. Because we played mostly for like the new Paramount News.
Oh, I see.
And then on stage we played a stage show.
I see. So it really was more or less what you might call a back-up band for whatever came up front?
Back-up band. And most of the time, like for a special band arrangement, you know in the show, we used a lot of stocks. Dave Peyton would -- stock arrangements.
